title: Latent prompting labbook — haruki 2028-06
content:
Quick goal: collect papers + quick takeaways about 'latent prompting' (compact learned vectors / small MLPs used as prompt proxies), record small experiments, and sketch evals for embed-to-kv techniques that might reduce active KV size in the serving runtime.

Context / motivation:
- For long-context or multi-turn products we care about keeping useful context available without exploding KV memory or per-token compute.
- Idea: store compressed "latent prompts" representing user/session history; expand them on-the-fly into short token sequences (or directly into activation-space keys) to feed into the model, reducing repeated prefix tokens.
- Prior work touches: prefix tuning, prompt tuning, adapter layers, and learned latent variable methods (seq-to-seq latents). Need to map those to practical inference runtimes (quantized MLPs, off-GPU cache).

Papers & takeaways (fast skim):
1) Paper A (prefix/prompt tuning family) — arXiv 2021-ish
   - Simple idea: learn continuous prefix vectors inserted at each layer.
   - For inference: inserting learned vectors every layer is expensive (activation reads/writes).
   - Takeaway: good proof-of-concept; but we want something that can be cached off-device and cheaply materialized.

2) Paper B (latent bottleneck for seq modeling) — arXiv 2023
   - Learn a small set of latent codes per context window, use cross-attention to inject them.
   - Pros: compresses long context into handful of vectors.
   - Cons: decoder cross-attention requires extra attention ops — tradeoff analysis needed.

3) Blog: 'Prompt Compaction with PCA' (community post)
   - Cheap baseline: compress prompt embedding vectors with PCA / SVD, store compressed coefficients, reconstruct at runtime.
   - Reconstruction cost: matmul with small basis matrix. Can be quantized and JITed.
   - Useful as baseline vs learned MLP compressor.

4) Engineering note: Serving-runtime constraints (from internal reading):
   - KV cache layout is optimized for beam of sequences; adding additional vectors should not blow up per-request latencies.
   - Latent approaches that require cross-attention per step may add ~10–30% per-token latency depending on implementation.
   - Prefetching/reconstruction in CPU host memory and streaming into GPU might hide some overhead.

My short experiments (local, tiny-llama-ish):
- Dataset: multi-turn demo convo logs (500 sessions).
- Baselines: full token prefix (keep last 100 tokens), PCA-compressed prefix (k=16), MLP-compressed latents (bottleneck=8).
- Implementation notes: saved per-session prefix embeddings from layers 6 and 12 (faster to extract). For PCA, fit on ~2k extracted vectors. For MLP, trained small encoder-decoder (2-layer MLP) to map aggregated token embeddings -> reconstructed 8-vector latent -> decode back to layer embedding space.

Results (very rough):
- PCA (k=16) reconstruction L2 vs full prefix: ~0.18 (normalized), MLP (8) L2: ~0.23 — qualitative: MLP tends to preserve conversational attributes (politeness, user idiosyncrasies) better.
- Downstream LM perplexity on continuation: PCA ~ +2% vs full prefix, MLP ~ +4% — acceptable for some UX scenarios where throughput matters.
- Latency: reconstruct-on-CPU (float32) adds ~6–9ms per request for tiny model; quantized int8 matmul reduced to ~2–3ms.

Open engineering questions / risks:
- Where to place the compression / reconstruction in the serving stack? Options:
  * Host CPU (prefetch, reconstruct, upload to GPU KV) — pros: frees GPU, cons: PCIe transfer cost + complexity.
  * On-GPU kernel (fused reconstruct + write to KV) — pros: lower PCIe overhead, cons: requires kernel change and more GPU cycles.
- Compatibility: must gracefully degrade to token-prefix fallback on mismatch or degraded reconstruction quality.
- Privacy/regulatory: storing compressed representations might still be PII-sensitive. Need same KMS/audit controls as raw KV.

Evaluation plan (next two sprints):
- Sprint 1 (prototype): implement PCA baseline in runtime shim; run throughput vs latency tests with sample workload (50% long-context requests). Measure tail latency and 99th percentile.
- Sprint 2 (quality & cost): train MLP compressor using more realistic logs, quantize to int8 with calibration, measure cost/token on hosted infra.
- Metrics: delta perplexity (vs token prefix), downstream task accuracy (3 tasks), cost per session, 95/99/99.9 latency, memory reduction %.

Notes for experiments / TODOs:
- [ ] Add reproducible script: export layer embeddings (layers 6/12), fit PCA, store basis as tiny model file.
- [ ] Bench: local synthetic QPS 200, measure GPU mem and token/sec.
- [ ] Check interaction with KV eviction — if reconstructed vector is slightly off, we should avoid thrashing evictions.
- [ ] Validate with LLM evals: prompt-injection stress tests, hallucination changes.

Brainstorm: alternative designs
- 'Latent-to-key' mapping: instead of reconstructing token-like embeddings, map latent vector directly to KV key/value pairs via learned linear maps; feed those into attention as if they were cached keys. That skips generation of tokens but requires exact key layout compatibility.
- 'Progressive expansion': keep very small latent (~4 vectors) active in hot cache; upon a longer request, asynchronously expand to fuller prefix in background and attach it when ready. UX: immediate low-quality but fast response, then subsequent turns improve.

Quick list of small experiments I want to run (short order):
- rebuild PCA baseline with int8 matmul (measure inference overhead)
- train latent->KV linear map and verify attention scores match original KV distribution (cosine similarity test)
- run human eval on 100 sessions: full-prefix vs PCA vs MLP latent to grade coherence and persona preservation

Questions for Owen / Mai:
- Owen: do we have a small kernel we can patch to test on-GPU reconstruction (experimental fuser)?
- Mai: can you sanity-check the privacy implications with security team — compressed vectors still PII? any precedent?

Misc notes / off-the-record thoughts:
- If the MLP compressor is small enough, we could ship it as a customer-side artifact (run in customer's VPC) to avoid sending raw conversation context to hosted preprocessors.
- Need a naming convention: 'latent-prompt-v{n}' with schema for serialization (version, layer-index, quant-scale).

References to follow up:
- list of concrete papers to read more deeply (add arXiv IDs here)
- link to internal perf benchmarks (JIRA-ML-1247)

End of labbook entry.

-- Haruki
